outline: This course focus on investigating the strength and deformability of jointed rock mass from analyzing the mechanical behavior of intact rock and discontinuities. Related issues for rock engineering such as numerical analysis, in-situ stress, rock hydraulics, and rock classification will be introduced, to help students understand the theory and the application of rock mechanics.
schedule:
Week 1 Introduction
Week 2 Stress and strain basics in rock mechanics
Week 3 Field investigation techniques, Rock classifications, Stereo projection
Week 4 Field investigation techniques, Rock classifications, Stereo projection
Week 5 Properties of intact rock
Week 6 Properties of intact rock
Week 7 Discontinuities in rock
Week 8 Discontinuities in rock
Week 9 Midterm exam
Week 10 Behavior of jointed rock masses
Week 11 Behavior of jointed rock masses
Week 12 In-situ stress
Week 13 Rock hydraulics
Week 14 Rock slope stability
Week 15 Tunnel and rock masses excavation
Week 16 Tunnel and rock masses excavation
Week 17 Numerical analysis in rock mechanics
Week 18 Final exam
assessment: Midterm exam (30%), Final exam (30%), Homework (30%), attendance (10%)
